## DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

Mathematical reasoning poses a significant challenge for language models due to its complex and structured nature. The paper introduces DeepSeekMath 7B, which continues pre-training DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B with 120B math-related tokens sourced from Common Crawl, together with natural language and code data.

### Key Results

DeepSeekMath 7B achieved an impressive score of 51.7% on the competition-level MATH benchmark without relying on external toolkits and voting techniques, approaching the performance level of Gemini-Ultra and GPT-4. Self-consistency over 64 samples from DeepSeekMath 7B achieves 60.9% on MATH.

### Key Contributions

The mathematical reasoning capability of DeepSeekMath is attributed to two key factors: First, it harnesses the significant potential of publicly available web data through a meticulously engineered data selection pipeline. Second, the authors introduce Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a variant of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), that enhances mathematical reasoning abilities while concurrently optimizing the memory usage of PPO.

The paper was published on February 5, 2024 (with final version on April 27, 2024) and is available on arXiv under the ID 2402.03300. You can access the full paper at https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03300.

## "Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization" by Leo Gao et al.

**Publication Details:**
- Authors: Leo Gao, John Schulman, Jacob Hilton
- Published at ICML'23 (the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning) on July 23, 2023
- arXiv version: arXiv:2210.10760, submitted October 19, 2022

**Main Contributions:**
The paper uses a synthetic setup where a fixed "gold-standard" reward model plays the role of humans. The researchers study how the gold reward model score changes as they optimize against the proxy reward model using either reinforcement learning or best-of-n sampling. They find that this relationship follows a different functional form depending on the method of optimization, and that in both cases its coefficients scale smoothly with the number of reward model parameters.

**Key Finding:**
Because the reward model is an imperfect proxy, optimizing its value too much can hinder ground truth performance, in accordance with Goodhart's law. This effect has been frequently observed, but not carefully measured due to the expense of collecting human preference data.

The paper is available on arXiv at https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.10760 and through the ICML proceedings.

## Paper Title
"RL Is Neither a Panacea Nor a Mirage: Understanding Supervised vs. Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning for LLMs"

## Authors and Affiliation
The paper is by Hangzhan Jin and colleagues from Polytechnique Montreal, Mila, McGill, and UDeM.

## arXiv Information
- **Paper ID:** 2508.16546
- **Posted:** August 22, 2025
- **Links:** 
  - Abstract: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16546
  - HTML: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16546v1
  - PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.16546

## Key Research Findings

The paper uses an out-of-distribution (OOD) variant of the 24-point card game and spectrum-based diagnostics to examine how supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement-learning fine-tuning (RL-FT) reshape model representation and OOD performance.

The key findings show that RL-FT can restore much of the OOD performance loss from SFT (e.g., Llama-11B 8.97% to 15.38%, Qwen-7B 17.09% to 19.66%), but when SFT induces severe overfitting and a clear distribution shift, RL-FT cannot fully recover OOD performance.

The researchers found that direction shifts of singular vectors matter more than singular value magnitudes, and that restoring singular vector directions for the top 20% of values or first 25% of layers recovers 70-80% of OOD performance.

## Overview

R1-RE reframes relation extraction as a reasoning task guided by annotation guidelines and introduces the first reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) framework for RE tasks, inspired by the workflow of human annotators.

## Problem and Approach

Traditional approaches typically frame RE as a supervised learning problem, directly mapping context to labels—an approach that often suffers from poor out-of-domain (OOD) generalization. ## Overview

The paper is arXiv preprint 2310.04373 titled "Confronting Reward Model Overoptimization with Constrained RLHF", authored by Ted Moskovitz and colleagues.

## Key Problem

Large language models are typically aligned with human preferences by optimizing reward models (RMs) fitted to human feedback. However, human preferences are multi-faceted, and it is increasingly common to derive reward from a composition of simpler reward models which each capture a different aspect of language quality. This presents a challenge, as it is difficult to appropriately weight these component RMs when combining them.

Because any RM is only a proxy for human evaluation, this process is vulnerable to overoptimization, wherein past a certain point, accumulating higher reward is associated with worse human ratings.

## Main Contributions

The paper performs the first study on overoptimization in composite RMs, showing that correlation between component RMs has a significant effect on the locations of these points.

The authors introduce a set of approaches for identifying and using these points as thresholds within a constrained optimization approach to RLHF. Their method addresses the problem of weighting component RMs by learning dynamic weights, naturally expressed by Lagrange multipliers. As a result, each RM stays within the range at which it is an effective proxy, improving evaluation performance.

The paper was published in October 2023 and has been cited in subsequent research on reward model optimization in RLHF.

## Entity-Aware Group Relative Policy Optimization (E-GRPO)

E-GRPO is a reinforcement learning framework developed to fine-tune LLM search agents using dense entity-aware rewards. 

E-GRPO is a novel RL framework that enhances policy optimization by formulating a dense, entity-aware reward function from the entities within the synthetic training data.

### Key Features

The paper presents a novel RL framework that integrates dense entity-aware rewards to provide granular feedback on LLM reasoning traces, formulating rewards based on normalized entity match rates and crediting near-miss reasoning with partial credit to enhance sample efficiency.

E-GRPO actively repurposes synthetic entity annotations embedded in question-answering tasks and complex research queries, leveraging ground-truth entity information for effective supervision.

### Advantages

E-GRPO exemplifies the utility of repurposing synthetic entity annotations as RL signals, sidestepping the annotation and computational overhead typical of Process Reward Models, and is computationally lightweight and annotation-free, using simple string match operations to compute dense rewards.

Empirical evaluations show E-GRPO significantly improves Pass@1 and Pass@3 metrics across QA and research tasks compared to standard GRPO.

The paper on E-GRPO is available on arXiv at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.24694.
